subject: Physics
stem: The speed of light in vacuum is taken as unity. If light takes 6 min 40 s to reach the Earth from the Sun, the distance between the Sun and the Earth in new unit is:
solution: Time, \(t = 6\) min \(40\) s \(= 360 + 40 = 400\) s. Distance in new system \(d = vt = 1 \times 400 = 400\).

subject: Physics
stem:
Match List I with List II:

| List I | List II |
|---|---|
| A. Young's Modulus | I. \(\dfrac{\Delta d}{\Delta L}\left(\dfrac{L}{d}\right)\) |
| B. Compressibility | II. \(\dfrac{FL}{A(\Delta L)}\) |
| C. Bulk Modulus | III. \(-\dfrac{1}{\Delta P}\left(\dfrac{\Delta V}{V}\right)\) |
| D. Poisson's Ratio | IV. \(-P\left(\dfrac{V}{\Delta V}\right)\) |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
solution: A. Young's Modulus \(= \dfrac{\text{Stress}}{\text{Strain}} = \dfrac{FL}{A\Delta L}\) (II). B. Compressibility \(= \dfrac{1}{\text{Bulk modulus}} = -\dfrac{1}{\Delta P}\left(\dfrac{\Delta V}{V}\right)\) (III). C. Bulk Modulus \(= -P\left(\dfrac{V}{\Delta V}\right)\) (IV). D. Poisson's Ratio \(= \dfrac{\text{Lateral strain}}{\text{Longitudinal strain}} = \dfrac{\Delta d}{\Delta L}\left(\dfrac{L}{d}\right)\) (I).

subject: Physics
stem: The current \(I\) in the circuit shown below is: (All diodes are ideal and identical). The circuit has four parallel branches between the terminals of a 10 V battery: a \(4\,\Omega\) resistor in series with a forward-biased diode, a \(3\,\Omega\) resistor in series with a reverse-biased diode, a forward-biased diode in series with a \(2\,\Omega\) resistor, and a reverse-biased diode in series with a \(5\,\Omega\) resistor.
solution: For an ideal diode, forward resistance \(= 0\) and reverse-biased resistance \(= \infty\). So only the \(4\,\Omega\) and \(2\,\Omega\) branches (with forward-biased diodes) conduct, in parallel across 10 V. \(I = \dfrac{10}{2} + \dfrac{10}{4} = \dfrac{30}{4} = \dfrac{15}{2}\) A.

subject: Physics
chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
stem: The angular speed of a flywheel is increased from 600 rpm to 1200 rpm in 10 s. The number of revolutions completed by the flywheel during this time is:
solution: \(\alpha = \dfrac{\omega_2 - \omega_1}{\Delta t} = \left(\dfrac{1200-600}{10}\right)\dfrac{2\pi}{60} = 2\pi\) rad/s\(^2\). With \(\omega_2 = 40\pi\), \(\omega_1 = 20\pi\), using \(\omega_2^2 = \omega_1^2 + 2\alpha\theta\): \((40\pi)^2 = (20\pi)^2 + 2(2\pi)\theta \Rightarrow \theta = 300\pi\) rad. Number of revolutions \(= \dfrac{\theta}{2\pi} = 150\).

subject: Physics
stem: For a simple pendulum, having time period \(T\), the variation of kinetic energy (K.E.) with time (\(t\)) is represented by:
options: K.E. sinusoidal, symmetric about a non-zero level, going below it
K.E. as a series of positive humps (\(\cos^2\)-like), touching zero at \(T/2\) and \(T\)
K.E. sinusoidal about zero, going negative
solution: Kinetic energy \(K = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}mA^2\omega^2\cos^2(\omega t + \phi)\). Therefore \(K \propto \cos^2(\omega t + \phi)\), a series of positive humps touching zero, so graph (3).

subject: Physics
stem: A resistor is connected to a battery of 12 V emf and internal resistance \(2\,\Omega\). If the current in the circuit is 0.6 A, the terminal voltage of the battery is:
solution: Terminal voltage of battery \(V = E - ir = 12 - 0.6 \times 2 = 10.8\) V.

subject: Physics
stem: A flask contains argon and chlorine in the ratio of 2 : 1 by mass. The temperature of the mixture is 27\(^\circ\)C. The ratio of root mean square speed of the molecules of the two gases \(\left(\dfrac{V_{rms}^{Ar}}{V_{rms}^{Cl}}\right)\) is: (Atomic mass of argon = 40.0 u and molecular mass of chlorine = 70.0 u)
solution: \(v_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}\). For same temperature, \(v_{rms} \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{M}}\). \(\dfrac{V_{rms}^{Ar}}{V_{rms}^{Cl}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{M_{Cl}}{M_{Ar}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{70}{40}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{7}}{2}\).

subject: Physics
stem: A ray of monochromatic light is passing through an equilateral prism (\(ABC\)) as shown in the figure. The refracted ray (\(QR\)) is parallel to its base (\(BC\)) and the angle of incidence (\(i\)) is 50\(^\circ\). Then the angle of deviation (\(\delta\)) is:
solution: Since \(QR\) is parallel to base, \(i = e\). Prism equation: \(i + e = A + \delta \Rightarrow 2i - A = \delta \Rightarrow 2(50) - 60 = \delta \Rightarrow \delta = 40^\circ\).

subject: Physics
chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
stem:
Match List I with List II.

| List-I | List-II |
|---|---|
| A. \(E = h\nu\) | I. de Broglie wavelength |
| B. Diffraction and Interference | II. Particle nature of light |
| C. \(\lambda = h/p\) | III. Wave nature of light |
| D. Compton effect | IV. Energy of photon |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
solution: A. \(E = h\nu\) is energy of photon (IV). B. Diffraction and interference confirm wave nature of light (III). C. \(\lambda = \dfrac{h}{p}\) is de Broglie wavelength of particle (I). D. Compton effect confirms particle nature of light (II).

subject: Physics
stem: In the first excited state of hydrogen atom, the energy of its electron is \(-3.4\) eV. The radial distance of the electron from the hydrogen nucleus in this case is approximately: (Take 1 eV = \(1.6 \times 10^{-19}\) J, e = \(1.6 \times 10^{-19}\) C and \(\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9 \times 10^9\) N m\(^2\)/C\(^2\))
solution: \(\dfrac{KQ^2}{2r} = 3.4\) eV \(\Rightarrow r = \dfrac{9\times10^9 \times (1.6\times10^{-19})^2}{2 \times 3.4 \times 1.6\times10^{-19}} = 2.1176\times10^{-10} \approx 2.1\times10^{-10}\) m.

subject: Physics
stem: A box of mass 15 kg is kept on the floor of a stationary trolley. The coefficient of static friction between the box and the trolley is 0.12. Keeping the box in stationary state over the trolley, the maximum acceleration with which the trolley can be moved horizontally in m s\(^{-2}\) is: (\(g = 10\) m/s\(^2\))
solution: For the box not to slip, the friction must provide its acceleration: \(a = \mu g = 0.12 \times 10 = 1.2\) m/s\(^2\).

subject: Physics
stem: Five capacitors of capacitances \(C_1 = C_2 = C_3 = C_4 = 10\,\mu\)F and \(C_5 = 2.5\,\mu\)F are connected as shown, along with a battery of 50 V. The equivalent capacitance and the charges on each capacitor respectively are:

subject: Physics
stem: The amount of work done to raise a mass '\(m\)' from the surface of the Earth to a height equal to the radius of the Earth '\(R\)' will be
solution: W.D. \(= U_2 - U_1 = -\dfrac{GMm}{R+R} - \left(-\dfrac{GMm}{R}\right) = -\dfrac{GMm}{2R} + \dfrac{GMm}{R} = \dfrac{GMm}{2R} = \dfrac{mgR}{2}\).

subject: Physics
stem: Each side of a metallic cube of mass 5.580 kg is measured to be 9.0 cm. Keeping the significant figures in view, the density of the material of the cube can be best expressed as \(X \times 10^3\) kg m\(^{-3}\) where the value of \(X\) is:
solution: Density \(= \dfrac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Volume}} = \dfrac{5.580\text{ kg}}{(9.0\text{ cm})^3} = \dfrac{5.580}{729}\times10^6 = 7.654\times10^3\) kg/m\(^3\). Keeping significant figures (side has 2 sig figs), \(= 7.7\times10^3\) kg/m\(^3\). Hence \(X = 7.7\).

subject: Physics
stem: The following plots show variation of velocity (\(v\)) with time (\(t\)) of a ball thrown vertically upward, and falling back. Which of the following plots is/are correct?
solution: During the whole journey, acceleration due to gravity is vertically downward. Therefore, the slope of the velocity vs time curve should be negative throughout the journey. A straight line with negative slope (starting positive, becoming negative) is graph C. Statement (C) is correct.

subject: Physics
stem: The sum of kinetic energy and potential energy of a simple pendulum bob is 0.02 joule. The speed of the simple pendulum bob at equilibrium position is approximately: (Consider mass of the bob = 20 g)
solution: At equilibrium position, total energy = K.E. \(\dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 = 0.02 \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{2}\times20\times v^2 \times10^{-3} = 2\times10^{-2} \Rightarrow v = \sqrt{2} = 1.41\) m/s.

subject: Physics
stem: In Young's double slit experiment, using monochromatic light of wavelength \(\lambda\), the intensity of light at a point on the screen where the path difference is \(\lambda\), is \(K\) units. The intensity of light at a point where the path difference is \(\dfrac{\lambda}{3}\) will be
solution: \(I = I_0\cos^2\dfrac{\Delta\phi}{2}\). For path difference \(\lambda\), \(K = I_0\cos^2\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda}\times\dfrac{\lambda}{2}\right) = I_0\). For path difference \(\dfrac{\lambda}{3}\): \(K_1 = I_0\cos^2\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda}\times\dfrac{\lambda}{3\times2}\right) = I_0\cos^2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{I_0}{4}\). So \(K_1 = \dfrac{K}{4}\).

subject: Physics
stem: In the circuit shown below, the voltage appearing across the diode \(D\) will be of the form: (An AC source \(V_i\) is connected to a diode \(D\) in series with a resistor \(R\); \(V_D\) is the voltage across the diode.)
options: One positive hump then flat (half-wave positive only)
solution: Voltage drop appears across the diode only when it is in reverse bias. In the positive half cycle the diode is reverse biased, so the output shows a positive hump in the positive half cycle and zero otherwise, giving graph (4).

subject: Physics
stem: An ac circuit contains a resistance of 1 k\(\Omega\), a capacitor of 0.1 \(\mu\)F and an inductor of 1 mH connected in series. The resonance frequency of the circuit is approximately:
solution: Resonance frequency \(f_0 = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{1\times10^{-7}\times10^{-3}}} = 15.9\) kHz.

subject: Physics
stem:
In interference and diffraction, the light energy is redistributed. If it reduces in one region, producing a dark fringe, it increases in another region, producing a bright fringe.
A. As there is no gain or loss of energy, these phenomena are consistent with the principle of conservation of energy.
B. Diffraction and interference are characteristics exhibited only by light waves.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A is true and B is also true
A is false, but B is true
A is true, but B is false
Both A and B are false
solution: In interference and diffraction there is no loss of energy, the energy gets redistributed (A is true). Interference and diffraction both are exhibited in light as well as sound waves (B is false).

subject: Physics
stem: For a travelling harmonic wave \(y(x, t) = 2.0\cos 2\pi(10t - 0.0080x + 0.35)\), where \(x\) and \(y\) are in cm and \(t\) in s. The phase difference between oscillatory motion of two points separated by a distance of 0.5 m is:
solution: Total phase \(\phi = 20\pi t - 2\pi \times 8\times10^{-3}x + 2\pi\times0.35\). \(\Delta\phi = k\Delta x = 2\pi\times8\times10^{-3}\Delta x = 2\pi\times8\times10^{-3}\times\left(\dfrac{100}{2}\right)\) (with \(\Delta x = 0.5\) m = 50 cm) \(= 8\pi\times10^{-1} = 0.8\pi\) rad.

subject: Physics
stem: The magnitude and direction of the acceleration produced in a body of mass 5 kg when two mutually perpendicular forces 8 N and 6 N act on it, are respectively:
solution: \(F_{net} = \sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = 10\) N. \(a = \dfrac{F_{net}}{m} = \dfrac{10}{5} = 2\) m/s\(^2\). \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{6}{8} \Rightarrow \theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)\) from the 8 N force.

subject: Physics
stem: Consider two uncharged capacitors of equal capacitance 200 pF. One of them is charged by a 100 V supply and disconnected. Now this capacitor is connected to the uncharged capacitor. The amount of electrostatic energy lost in the process is:
solution: Energy loss \(= \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{C_1 C_2}{C_1 + C_2}V^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{200\times200}{400}\right)\times10^{-12}(100)^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}\times10^6\times10^{-12} = 0.5\times10^{-6}\) J.

subject: Physics
stem: The power of a crane, which lifts a mass of 1000 kg to a height of 20 m in 10 s is: (\(g = 9.8\) m/s\(^2\))
solution: Power \(= \dfrac{\text{Work}}{\text{Time}} = \dfrac{mgh}{t} = \dfrac{10^3\times9.8\times20}{10} = 19.6\) kW.

subject: Physics
stem: In a vernier calliper, 20 VSD coincide with 16 MSD (each division of length 1 mm). The least count of the vernier callipers is:

subject: Physics
stem:
When a ruler falls vertically, 5 different persons catch it with different reaction times. (\(g = 9.8\) m s\(^{-2}\))
A. Person A has reaction time of 0.20 s.
B. Person B has reaction time of 0.22 s.
C. Person C has reaction time of 0.18 s.
D. Person D has reaction time of 0.19 s.
E. Person E has reaction time of 0.21 s.
What is the correct order of the distance travelled by the ruler for each person?
solution: Distance covered \(= \dfrac{1}{2}gt^2\), so larger reaction time gives larger distance. Descending order of reaction time: \(t_B > t_E > t_A > t_D > t_C\). Therefore descending order of distance covered: \(S_B > S_E > S_A > S_D > S_C\).

subject: Physics
stem: A uniform metallic wire having resistance \(4\,\Omega\) is bent to form a square loop (\(ABCD\)) (see figure). A resistance of \(2\,\Omega\) is connected between points \(B\) and \(D\) and a battery of 2 V is connected across points \(A\) and \(C\) as shown in the figure. Now the value of current (\(I\)) is:
solution: Each side of the square has resistance \(1\,\Omega\). This forms a balanced Wheatstone bridge, so no current flows through the \(2\,\Omega\) resistance connected between \(B\) and \(D\). Effective resistance across \(AC\): \([R_{effective}]_{AC} = 1\,\Omega\). \(I = \dfrac{E}{R_{eff}} = \dfrac{2}{1} = 2\) A.

subject: Physics
stem: A room heater is rated 400 W, 220 V. If the supply voltage drops to 200 V, what will be the power consumed (approximately)?
solution: Rated power \(P_0 = \dfrac{V_0^2}{R}\); consumed power \(P_c = \dfrac{V^2}{R}\). So \(P_c = \left(\dfrac{V}{V_0}\right)^2 P_0 = \left(\dfrac{200}{220}\right)^2 \times 400 = 331\) W.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Magnetic Field of Coil and Magnetic Moment
stem: A 100-turn closely wound circular coil of radius 5 cm has a magnetic field of \(3.14 \times 10^{-3}\) T at its centre. The current flowing through the coil, and the magnitude of the magnetic moment of this coil are, respectively: (Take \(\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\) T m/A)
solution: Magnetic field of circular loop: \(B_0 = \dfrac{\mu_0 N i}{2R}\). \(i = \dfrac{2RB_0}{\mu_0 N} = \dfrac{2\times5\times10^{-2}\times3.14\times10^{-3}}{4\pi\times10^{-7}\times100} = 2.5\) A. Magnetic moment \(M = NiA = 100\times2.5\times3.14\times(5\times10^{-2})^2 = 2\) A m\(^2\).

subject: Physics
stem: A rectangular wire loop of sides 8 cm and 3 cm with a small cut, is moving out of a region of uniform magnetic field of magnitude 0.3 T directed normal to the plane of the loop. The emf developed across the cut, if the velocity of the loop is 2 cm s\(^{-1}\), in a direction normal to the shorter side of the loop, will be:
solution: Induced emf across the shorter side \(E_{induced} = Bvl = 0.3 \times 2\times10^{-2} \times 3\times10^{-2} = 1.8\times10^{-4}\) V.

subject: Physics
stem:
Four statements are given (\(A\) is mass number):
A. The volume of a nucleus is proportional to \(A^{1/3}\).
B. The volume of a nucleus is proportional to \(A\).
C. The difference in mass of an atom and its nucleus is called the mass defect.
D. The difference in mass of a nucleus and its constituents is called the mass defect.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A and C are true, but B and D are false
B and C are true, but A and D are false
A and D are true, but B and C are false
B and D are true, but A and C are false
solution: Size of nucleus \(r = r_0 A^{1/3} \Rightarrow r^3 = r_0^3 A \Rightarrow V \propto A\) (since \(V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3\)). So A is wrong and B is correct. The difference between the actual mass of a nucleus and its constituents is called the mass defect, so C is wrong and D is correct.

subject: Physics
stem: An unknown nucleus has a nuclear density of \(2.29 \times 10^{17}\) kg/m\(^3\) and mass of \(19.926 \times 10^{-27}\) kg. Its mass number \(A\) is approximately: (Take \(R_0 = 1.2 \times 10^{-15}\) m, \(4\pi = 12.56\))
solution: Using volume \(= \dfrac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Density}}\): \(\dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = \dfrac{M}{\rho}\) with \(R = R_0 A^{1/3}\), so \(\dfrac{4}{3}\pi R_0^3 A = \dfrac{M}{\rho}\). \(A = \dfrac{M}{\rho}\times\dfrac{3}{4\pi R_0^3} = \dfrac{19.926\times10^{-27}\times3}{2.29\times10^{17}\times12.56\times(1.2\times10^{-15})^3} \approx 12\).

subject: Physics
stem: Savitha, a XI standard student, while conducting an experiment to determine the effective length of a simple pendulum \(L\), notes down the data of time taken to complete 30 oscillations as 60 s and hence calculates the length of the simple pendulum as: (Take \(\pi^2 = 9.8\), and \(g = 9.8\) m/s\(^2\))
solution: Time period \(T = \dfrac{60}{30} = 2\) s. \(T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g}} \Rightarrow l = \dfrac{gT^2}{4\pi^2} = \dfrac{9.8\times2\times2}{4\times9.8} = 1\) m.

subject: Physics
stem: An electric heater supplies heat to a system at a rate of 100 W. If the system performs work at a rate of 75 J/s, then the rate at which internal energy increases will be:
solution: Using the first law of thermodynamics \(Q = \Delta U + W\), rate form: \(\dfrac{dQ}{dt} = \dfrac{d(\Delta U)}{dt} + \dfrac{dW}{dt}\). \(100 = \dfrac{d(\Delta U)}{dt} + 75 \Rightarrow \dfrac{d(\Delta U)}{dt} = 25\) W.

subject: Physics
chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
stem: A thin wire of length '\(L\)' and linear mass density '\(m\)' is bent into a circular ring (in \(x\)-\(y\) plane) with centre '\(C\)' as shown in figure. The moment of inertia of the ring about an axis \(yy'\) (a tangent to the ring parallel to the \(y\)-axis) will be:
solution: Mass of wire \(M = mL\). \(L = 2\pi r \Rightarrow r = \dfrac{L}{2\pi}\). Using parallel axis theorem, \(I_{yy'} = I_{CM} + Mr^2 = \dfrac{Mr^2}{2} + Mr^2 = \dfrac{3}{2}Mr^2 = \dfrac{3}{2}(mL)\left(\dfrac{L}{2\pi}\right)^2 = \dfrac{3mL^3}{8\pi^2}\).

subject: Physics
stem: A galvanometer of resistance \(100\,\Omega\) gives full scale deflection for a current of 1 mA. It is converted into an ammeter of range 0 – 10 A. The shunt required is:
solution: \(i_G = 1\) mA \(= 0.001\) A; \(i_s = 10 - i_G \approx 10\) A. Shunt and galvanometer are in parallel: \(i_s r_s = i_G R_G \Rightarrow 10 \times r_s = 0.001 \times 100 \Rightarrow r_s = 0.01\,\Omega\).

subject: Physics
stem: In a metre bridge experiment (see figure), the positions of the cell, \(E\), and galvanometer, \(G\), are interchanged. We shall observe in the galvanometer:
options: There will be no deflection irrespective of the position of the jockey
Both right-sided and left-sided deflection and at balance point, no deflection
solution: The position of the null point will not change when the galvanometer (\(G\)) and the cell (\(E\)) are interchanged. There will be no deflection in the galvanometer only at the balance point. In an unbalanced metre bridge, if \(E\) and \(G\) are interchanged, the deflection may be towards the left-side or the right-side.

subject: Physics
stem: The peak value of an alternating current is 5 A and frequency is 60 Hz. How long will the current, starting from zero, take to reach the peak value?
solution: \(i = i_{peak}\sin(\omega t)\), where \(\omega = 2\pi f = 2\pi\times60 = 120\pi\) rad/s. \(i = 5\sin(120\pi t)\). At peak, \(5 = 5\sin(120\pi t) \Rightarrow \sin(120\pi t) = 1 = \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) \Rightarrow 120\pi t = \dfrac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow t = \dfrac{1}{240}\) s.

subject: Physics
stem: The figure given below shows a long straight solid wire of circular cross-section of radius '\(a\)' carrying steady current \(I\). The current \(I\) is uniformly distributed across its cross-section. The plot which correctly represents the variation of magnetic field (\(B\)) with distance (\(r\)) from the axis of the conductor in the region is:
options: \(B\) rises linearly from 0 to a peak at \(r = a\), then falls as \(1/r\)
\(B\) is zero up to \(r = a\), jumps to a peak at \(a\), then falls as \(1/r\)
\(B\) starts at a non-zero value, slightly rises to a peak at \(a\), then falls
\(B\) rises non-linearly (concave) to a peak at \(r = a\), then falls as \(1/r\)
solution: For a long straight solid wire carrying steady current uniformly distributed: for \(r < a\), \(B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I r}{2\pi a^2} \Rightarrow B \propto r\) (linear rise). For \(r > a\), \(B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r} \Rightarrow B \propto \dfrac{1}{r}\) (falls). This corresponds to plot (1).

subject: Physics
stem:
Two statements are given below:
A. When the forward bias voltage across a p-n junction diode increases above a certain threshold voltage, the diode current increases significantly.
B. This current is called reverse saturation current.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statements A and B are true
Statement A is true, but Statement B is false
Both Statements A and B are false
Statement A is false, but Statement B is true
solution: When forward bias voltage increases beyond the threshold voltage, the diode current increases significantly (A is true). This is not the reverse saturation current (B is false).

subject: Physics
stem:
Which of the following statements are correct?
A. Inside a conductor, the electrostatic field is zero.
B. Electric field at the surface of a charged conductor does not depend on its surface charge density.
C. The interior of a charged conductor can have no excess charge in the static situation.
D. At the surface of a charged conductor, the electrostatic field must be normal to the surface at every point.
E. The electrostatic potential is zero everywhere inside a charged conductor.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
solution: A. Electrostatic field is zero inside a conductor (true). B. Electric field at the surface \(= \dfrac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}\hat{n}\) depends on surface charge density \(\sigma\) (so B is false). C. The interior of a charged conductor cannot have any excess charge in the static situation (true). D. At the surface, the electrostatic field is normal to the surface (true). E. The electrostatic potential is constant and can be non-zero everywhere inside a charged conductor (so E is false). Correct: A, C and D.

subject: Physics
chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
stem: For a metal of work function 6.6 eV, which of the following wavelengths of incident radiation does not give rise to the photoelectric effect? (Take Planck's constant as \(6.6 \times 10^{-34}\) J s)
solution: Photoelectric effect doesn't occur when \(\dfrac{hc}{\lambda} < \) work function, i.e. \(\lambda > \dfrac{hc}{W_0} = \dfrac{6.6\times10^{-34}\times3\times10^8}{6.6\times1.6\times10^{-19}} = \dfrac{3\times10^{-7}}{1.6} = \dfrac{300}{1.6}\) nm \(= 187.5\) nm. So for \(\lambda > 187.5\) nm no photoelectric effect occurs; option (3) 200 nm is correct.

subject: Physics
stem: In a concave lens, a ray of light emanating from the object parallel to the principal axis of the lens after refraction:
options: passes through \(2F\), which is the radius of curvature of the lens.
appears to diverge from the first principal focus.
emerges parallel to the principal axis.
passes through the second principal focus.
solution: For a concave (diverging) lens, a ray parallel to the principal axis after refraction appears to diverge from the second principal focus \(F_2\) (virtual image position for object at infinity). The official answer is marked (2*), noting the best appropriate answer is option (2), although it should be the second principal focus.

subject: Physics
stem: A submarine is designed to withstand an absolute pressure of 100 atm. How deep can it go below the water surface? (Consider the density of water = 1000 kg m\(^{-3}\), 1 atm = \(1 \times 10^5\) Pa and gravitational acceleration \(g = 10\) m/s\(^2\))
solution: \(P = P_0 + \rho g h \Rightarrow 100\times10^5 = 10^5 + 10^3\times10\times h \Rightarrow 10^7 = 10^5 + 10^4 h \Rightarrow 10^3 = 10 + h \Rightarrow h = 1000 - 10 = 990\) m.

subject: Physics
stem:
Match List I with List II:

| List-I (Electromagnetic wave) | List-II (Production) |
|---|---|
| A. Microwave | I. Electrons in atoms emit light when they move from a higher energy level to a lower energy level |
| B. Visible light | II. Radioactive decay of nucleus |
| C. Gamma rays | III. Vibration of atoms and molecules |
| D. Infra-red rays | IV. Klystron valve or magnetron valve |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
solution: A. Microwave — Klystron valve or magnetron valve (IV). B. Visible light — Electrons in atoms emit light when they move from a higher energy level to a lower energy level (I). C. Gamma rays — Radioactive decay of nucleus (II). D. Infra-red rays — Vibration of atoms and molecules (III).
